Mozambique's Civil Registration Code (Law 12/2018) establishes the e-SIRCEV electronic civil registration system explicitly 'integrated with national ID and health systems' (crvslaws.org). revised_comments: Mozambique's electronic civil registration and vital statistics system (e-SIRCEV), established under the revised Civil Registration Code (Law 12/2018), is integrated with the national ID and health systems. Since July 2024, e-SIRCEV interoperates in real time with the Hospital Data Management Module for Births (MGDH-births), initially deployed across health facilities in Inhambane province and expanding, with nationwide rollout planned. Integration remains partial rather than nationwide.

revision_notes: Original 0/Unknown refined to 1 (No). Mozambique's social protection beneficiary system is managed by INAS through its own Beneficiary Registration System and e-INAS platform, which issues INAS-specific beneficiary ID cards rather than relying on the national ID system. A World Bank case study (Webster, Risso Brandon & Zaldivar Chimal, 2023) notes that roughly one third of the population lacks a national ID card and that there is no national ID authority registry, with the central bank instead issuing 'comfort letters' allowing INAS beneficiary cards (not the national ID) to be used to open payment accounts for beneficiaries. This confirms the social registry uses its own identifier rather than the national ID system.
revised_comments: Mozambique's social protection beneficiary registry, managed by the National Institute of Social Action (INAS) through its Beneficiary Registration System and e-INAS platform, issues its own beneficiary identification cards rather than relying on the national ID system for identification and deduplication. Given national ID coverage gaps, the central bank has permitted INAS beneficiary cards as an alternative form of identification for opening payment accounts.
